desc.en: A campaign concept built on digital fatigue — with no lecturing and no second helping of “detox”.
desc.pl: Koncept kampanii oparty na cyfrowym zmęczeniu — bez moralizowania i bez kolejnego komunikatu o „detoksie”.

blocks.title: IKEA Offline
blocks.lede: A campaign about what home gives us that a screen never can.

items.label: Role
items.value: Concept, communication strategy, art direction, campaign design

items.label: Scope
items.value: Campaign platform, key visual, adaptation system, channel extensions, copy system

items.statement: Everyone was telling people to put the phone down.
body: I didn’t think IKEA needed to join them.

Digital-fatigue advertising was already full of detox language and guilt: spend less time on your screen, switch off, be more present. That felt slightly wrong for a brand whose job is to make everyday life better — not to tell people they’re living badly.
So I turned the problem around. What if IKEA didn’t have to fight the phone at all? What if it simply reminded people what home can feel like when nobody is performing for a screen?
Not in the headline, not in the visual, not as a comparison.

Instead, it lives in the small moments that make you forget to check anything: dinner stretching longer than planned, collapsing into a sofa after a long day, talking without needing a reason, closing your eyes for a minute.

blocks.text: Don’t tell people to put the phone down. Give them something worth forgetting it for.

body: I developed the concept as a complete campaign platform: communication strategy, key visual, copy system, adaptation rules and channel extensions.
The idea started with pencil and paper, then moved into visual development with Google Stitch and Krea before being assembled in Figma.
This was made as a spec project, so the test wasn’t client approval or campaign data. It was whether one observation could survive as a real campaign system.
That’s the part I care about most: finding a simple human truth, giving it one strong creative rule, and letting the work stay quiet enough for the idea to breathe.
